events.title: Drop signal fired: Bitcoin is -8.3% over 7 days

messages.text:
**Daily Market Summary · 11 November 2026**

**Alert**
• **Drop signal fired: Bitcoin is -8.3% over 7 days.** A Rally watch drop window is now open. In our past data, trading and new sign-ups usually slowed in the two weeks after such a signal: hold promotions, lead with trust.

**Snapshot**
• Bitcoin is about $73,800, down about 8% over 7 days.
• Headline label: BULLISH, medium confidence (66). The long-run uptrend still holds, but price is only about 1% above its 200-day average.
• Fear & Greed is 29 (fear).

**What happened (last 24h)**
• Bitcoin fell below $73,000 during the day after US October inflation came in above expectations (0.4% for the month), and Fed officials Logan and Bowman said they may back more rate rises (PANews).
• About $382M of bets placed across the market were forced to close in 24 hours, mostly bets on a rise (PANews). US Bitcoin ETFs saw about $487M flow out.

**Short-term outlook (next 1-7 days)**
The near term looks soft: the mood is fearful and price has been under its 50-day average for 21 days.
• Turns up: a close above $75,250 (top of a typical week's swing), then $81,141 (50-day average).
• Sideways: between $73,123 and $75,250; a normal week swings about $2,957.
• Turns down: a close below $73,123 (200-day average), then $67,706 (200-week average).
• Rally watch: drop window open. A rally signal would need about $86,944; the drop signal stays on while price is below about $74,064.
• Scheduled: next Fed meeting, 8 December.

**News that matters**
• US inflation above expectations (PANews): short term, moderate negative.
• Fed officials back more rate rises (PANews): medium term, moderate negative.
• Goldman Sachs, Citi and others commit about $270M to a joint stablecoin project (PANews): long term, small positive.

**Altcoins & themes**
• Most large coins are down 3-4% in 24 hours; ZEC fell about 11% even as Grayscale pledged $1M to its ecosystem, and the reports give no clear reason (PANews).
• New on Reku: according to the project, Babylon's proposal to bring native Bitcoin as collateral to Aave passed with a 100% vote (10 Nov).

**Bigger picture**
• The next month is mixed and leaning softer until price wins back $81,141 (50-day average); the 3-6 month picture still leans up while Bitcoin holds above $73,123 (200-day average).

Dashboard: https://andrifa.github.io/crypto-market-state-dashboard/

**Digital / Paid:** A Rally watch drop window opened today and Bitcoin is down about 8% in a week, so hold any step-up in active-trader campaigns until a close back above $81,141 (the 50-day average) and keep a budget reserve. Apply the d30 ROI stop-loss on running campaigns while the window is open. For new and stablecoin audiences, lean creatives on trust and learning (Fear & Greed is 29); keep rally creatives ready in case a rally signal comes near $86,944.

**Social media & content:** Keep the normal posting rhythm but switch tone to calm, safety-first content. Post a plain explainer on why Bitcoin fell (US inflation came in above expectations and Fed officials talked about more rate rises, per PANews), without saying where price goes next. Add a short 'how we protect your assets' post: Across, Initia and Arcus all reported security incidents yesterday (PANews). For a calmer long-run topic, use Goldman Sachs and Citi committing about $270M to a joint stablecoin project.

**CRM:** No promotional pressure while the drop window is open. Send existing holders a calm note that prices fell about 8% this week after hotter US inflation, with a link to an explainer and no push to trade, and remind users how to turn on two-step login and spot fake support accounts. Keep welcome and education journeys running and have the post-rally onboarding journey ready, since new sign-ups and first deposits tend to arrive 2-4 weeks after a rally.

**SEO:** Pluang ran 60 short items on 11 Nov and Pintu 65 posts on 6-10 Nov (51 of them daily stock price pages); Indodax was not readable today. High-priority topics: (1) Bitcoin's fall after hot US inflation, covered by Pluang: refresh 'why is Bitcoin down today' with the inflation and Fed context; (2) Fed rate rises, Pluang covers Deutsche Bank's call for three hikes: publish a plain 'what a Fed rate rise means for crypto' explainer ahead of the 8 December meeting; (3) tokenized stocks, covered by Pintu and Pluang (NYSE choosing Avalanche): update the tokenized-stocks guide. Also refresh the account-security guide after this week's hacks. Check each against Reku's pages first. https://andrifa.github.io/crypto-market-state-dashboard/

**Altcoins:** Most large coins fell 3-4% in 24 hours after the US inflation data (ETH -3.8%, SOL -3.8%, XRP -3.9%). ZEC fell about 11% even as Grayscale pledged $1M to the Zcash ecosystem; the reports give no clear reason (PANews). Banks and payment firms keep building on stablecoins: Goldman Sachs and Citi committed about $270M to a joint project and Visa added Monad (MON -0.9%) to its settlement network (PANews). New on Reku: according to the project, Babylon's proposal for native Bitcoin collateral on Aave passed with a 100% vote; Pons (PONS) is down about 29% in 7 days with no stated reason.
